content.title: Convert Image to Base64 String
content.p1: Developers and web designers often need to embed images directly into HTML or CSS files to reduce HTTP requests.
content.p2: Our Image to Base64 Converter encodes your image file into a long string of characters that represents the binary data. You can paste this string straight into your code.

features.title: Key Features
features.f1_desc: One-click copy. We format the output for HTML (`<img src="...">`) or CSS (`background: url(...)`).
features.f2_desc: Embedding small icons and logos as Base64 eliminates the network overhead of fetching external image files.
features.f3_desc: Works with PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, SVG, and even ICO files.
features.subtitle: Essential for developers and designers.

how_to.title: How to use?
how_to.step2_desc: The tool immediately converts the file to a Data URI.
how_to.step3_desc: Click "Copy to Clipboard" to grab the code.
how_to.step4_desc: Insert it into your `src` attribute or CSS file.
how_to.subtitle: Simple steps to encode your images.

use_cases.title: When to use Base64?
list: Small Images: Best for icons, spinners, and small logos (under 10KB).
Single-File Apps: When you need to bundle everything into one HTML file (e.g., email templates).
Offline Access: Ensures images load even without a network connection if the HTML is saved locally.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: Base64 is a way to represent binary data (like images) using only printable text characters. This allows you to embed images directly into code files.
faq.q2: Will this increase the file size?
faq.a2: Yes, Base64 encoding typically increases the file size by about 33%. It is recommended only for small images (icons, logos) to avoid performance issues.
faq.a3: Data URIs are supported by all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) and IE8+.
faq.a4: Yes, the conversion happens entirely in your browser. Your images are never uploaded to our servers.
faq.a5: Technically yes, but it's not recommended. Large Base64 strings can bloat your HTML/CSS and slow down page rendering.
